newsitem.title: GERMANY: German firms balk at Lufthansa air-miles scheme.
newsitem.headline: German firms balk at Lufthansa air-miles scheme.

text.p: Several large German companies have told Deutsche Lufthansa AG they are unhappy with its "Miles and More" air-miles programme because it distorted competition in the German air travel market.

Metals and trading group Metalgesellschaft AG on Monday confirmed a magazine report that it and several other large users were unhappy with the scheme, which allows passengers to build up credits towards future tickets.
"We want to discuss this with Lufthansa. They know our position on this and it is up to them now to respond," a spokesman for Metalgesellschaft said.

A report in the magazine "Der Spiegel" had earlier said that a number of large corporate users were unhappy that Lufthansa's air-miles programme meant it was frequently being chosen by staff for corporate travel ahead cheaper rivals.
The companies themselves do not benefit greatly from the scheme because employees tend to take the bonus air-miles for their own personal use.

Metallgesellschaft said it had held meetings with other companies dissatisfied with the scheme, including chemical group Degussa AG, engineering giant Siemens AG and Commerzbank, Germany's third largest bank.

If large corporate users started moving away from Lufthansa, it would damage revenues that have already come under pressure from increased competition in its domestic market from airlines including British Airways Plc and Air France.
"We are not out to harm Lufthansa, however," the Metallgesellschaft spokesman said.

A Lufthansa spokeswoman said that the move was "a questionable initiative by a handful of companies" and noted that a large number of corporate users were happy with the scheme, which was introduced four years ago.
